data: © Soviet Academy of Sciences (historical). Lunokhod 1 location confirmed in 2010 by NASA Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter imagery.

The first remote-controlled rover to operate on another world. Drove 10.5 km over 322 days, photographing over 20,000 images. Lost to history until 2010, when the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter spotted it from orbit — still sitting exactly where it stopped.
First teleoperated rover — established the architecture every Mars rover from Sojourner to Perseverance has built on.

Luna 17 landed in Mare Imbrium on November 17, 1970 — and deployed Lunokhod 1, the first wheeled vehicle to operate on another world, beating NASA's LRV by seven months. Lunokhod 1 drove 10.5 km over 11 lunar days, controlled by a five-person team in Crimea. Returned 25,000 photographs and 211 panoramas before going silent in September 1971.
First wheels on the Moon — Lunokhod 1
Lunokhod 1 — 8-wheeled, 756 kg, solar-powered chassis with a polonium-210 RTG for nighttime warmth. Designed for 3 months, lasted 10.
Luna 17 lander + ramps for Lunokhod 1 deployment. The Soviet remote-control team operated from a converted submarine on the Crimean coast.
Lunokhod 1 driving on Mare Imbrium — controlled by a five-person team in real time despite the 2.5 second light-speed delay each way.
Lunokhod 1 traverse map — 10.5 km zigzag across Mare Imbrium, with science stops at rocks and craters.
Lunokhod 1 retroreflector — still used by Earth-based lunar-laser-ranging stations today, 50+ years later.
Orrery reference map of LROC imagery and the Lunokhod 1 traverse data

Illustrated block map of the Luna 17 landing site in Mare Imbrium: the Luna 17 lander stands at the centre, and the looping route of Lunokhod 1 passes a bright crater and ends at the rover’s last position.
